text: Before a single dbt model exists, this platform needs to decide who can do what. This lesson sets up the warehouses and roles everything else is built on.

Two warehouses, sized for two different jobs: transforming_wh for dbt builds, and reporting_wh for Power BI and analyst queries. Separate compute means a heavy dbt build never makes a business user's report wait in a queue.

Every Snowflake account ships with a built-in role hierarchy. ACCOUNTADMIN sits on top, encapsulating SECURITYADMIN and SYSADMIN, and SYSADMIN is the real parent almost every custom role gets slotted under.

This platform creates two custom roles: TRANSFORMER, which dbt runs as everywhere, and ANALYST, a deliberately narrower read-only role. Both get granted up to SYSADMIN, and each gets usage on exactly one warehouse — never the other's.
Deciding this now, in SQL, before a single model exists, is what makes governed a fact about the platform instead of a hope about how people will behave. Next: loading the real raw data.
